sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year, from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203].
Operating income compounded faster at 12.3% [F204], lifting operating margin from 3.2% in FY2017 [F23] to 3.9% in FY2026 [F32].
Growth stepped up in FY2021 (17.5% [D189]) and FY2022 (15.8% [D238]), which the filings tie to comparable sales up 16% [P56] and 14% [P42], plus new warehouses.
FY2026 growth of 10.1% [D434] rested on comparable sales up 8%, from a 5% rise in average ticket and 3% in shopping frequency [P14], with product sales adding 9.9pp [D535].
Warehouse ancillary and other businesses was the largest single contributor at +3.7pp [D601], growing 19.9% [D600] to 20.2% of revenue [D599].
The cited filing text does not explain that ancillary growth; it only notes these businesses grew faster than core merchandise [P12].
Operating income grew 12.5% [D435] against revenue growth of 10.1% [D434], an incremental margin of 4.7% [D457] above the 3.9% average [F32].
Diluted EPS grew 14.0% [D438], just ahead of net income at 13.9% [D436], as diluted shares fell 0.1% [D452].
Operating margin of 3.9% [F32] equals its window high [D691] and sits above the 3.4% median [D692] and the 3.1% low [D690].
FY2026 operating margin rose 0.1pp [D447] with SG&A leverage of 0.1pp [D460] and no cost-of-revenue effect [D459].
Net margin of 3.0% [F52] sits 0.9pp below operating margin [F32], with the effective tax rate at 24.7% [D420].

In FY2022 cost of revenue took 0.7pp [D263] and SG&A returned 0.7pp [D264], because gross margin fell 65 basis points on lower core merchandise margins and a LIFO charge [P40], while SG&A fell 77 basis points on sales leverage [P38].
FY2026 gross margin included $174 of IEEPA tariff refunds booked against merchandise costs [P15], against operating income of $11.7 billion [F22].

FY2026 operating cash flow of $15.8 billion [F82] was 1.71x net income of $9.23 billion [D421][F42], and free cash flow of $9.38 billion [F102] was 1.02x net income [D422], above the 0.99x window median [D701].
The filing credits the FY2026 cash rise to higher operating income and faster inventory turns [P6], with operating cash flow up 18.6% [D439] and inventory up 6.7% [D456].
Capex of $6.44 billion [F92] ran at 2.41x D&A of $2.67 billion [X50][D423], while the free cash flow margin of 3.1% [D418] sat above its 2.8% window median [D698].
The FY2022 conversion trough, with free cash flow at 0.60x net income [D226] and down 34.8% [D244], is not explained by the cited passage, which stops before naming its working-capital drivers [P35].
Net cash rose to $15.1 billion [D427], 5.0% of revenue [D428], ranking at the 100th percentile of six retail peers [D715] against a peer median of -4.4% [D716].
The current ratio of 1.06x [F182] sits above its 1.02x window median [D704], and cash and investments of $21.3 billion [D425] cover total debt of $6.16 billion [D426].

Long-term debt fell 31.5% [D445] to $3.91 billion [F192], but the current portion rose to $2.25 billion from $75.0 million [X160][X159], lifting total debt 6.5% [D454]; the cited filings do not explain the reclassification.
Shareholder payouts were $848 million of buybacks [X110] and $2.46 billion of dividends [X120], 35.2% of free cash flow [D430], under a $4 billion authorisation with $1,115 million left [P3].

FY2026 includes $174 of one-off IEEPA tariff refunds recorded against merchandise costs [P15], against operating income of $11.7 billion [F22], and three basis points of gross margin net of member price cuts [P12].
Because these refunds do not recur, the 3.9% margin [F32] overstates the run-rate by a small amount.
FY2022 free cash flow conversion fell to 0.60x net income [D226], the window low [D699], but recovered to 1.07x in FY2023 [D275], so the dip lasted one year.

FY2024 shareholder payouts reached 146.9% of free cash flow [D332] with dividends of $9.04 billion [X118]; net cash fell to $5.25 billion in FY2024 [D329] from $8.78 billion in FY2023 [D280], and the cited passages do not explain the FY2024 dividend.
Operating margin holding at or above its 3.9% level [F32] and window high [D691] in the FY2027 10-K would confirm the trend, while a fall toward the 3.4% median [D692] would reverse it.
Free cash flow to net income falling below the 0.99x window median [D701] in the FY2027 10-K would show conversion slipping back toward the 0.60x FY2022 low [D699].

The $4 billion buyback authorisation expires in January 2027 with $1,115 million remaining [P3]; repurchases staying near the $848 million of FY2026 [X110] in the FY2027 10-K would keep the share count flat.
